The closest match is a paper by Feiyu Zhou on wind-induced bridge response forecasting and bridge structural health monitoring. It uses a transformer-based forecasting model on real measurements from the Hardanger Bridge and says the approach can support digital twin monitoring and early-warning detection of structural change [1].

It is not specifically about wind bridge forecasting in the sense of bridge wind load prediction alone; rather, it forecasts structural response under wind excitation and compares predicted and measured vibrations [1]. The other papers focus on wind power, weather nowcasting, or urban wind prediction, not bridge forecasting [2-10].
